questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew that Sorbonne University was a university that was well known around the world. I also liked that I could develop my French language skills while being there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It took a lot of emails back and forward to get the information that I needed. The catalogue with their courses is hard to find and they don't offer a lot of English courses. I was allowed to be part of a master program where they spoke English but as I understand it it is not everyone that is allowed to take part of their master courses. 
When I was first registered as a part of Sorbonne I got all the emails from a coordinator at Sorbonne and that worked very well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There is an exchange office at Sorbonne that provided me with a lot of help. There is also a coordinator that helped me a lot through email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I lived at Fondation Danoise in cite universitaire in the 14th arrondissement. You have to apply directly to them and I think they get a lot of application but it was a very nice place. It was only 4,5 kilometers by bike and 30 min by tram and metro to the university. 
I also got offered a place in another house in cite universitaire through Sorbonne that I said no to. I think they prioritise exchange students pretty high at Sorbonne when it comes to housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: For me it worked great. I lot of the people I lived with also studied at Sorbonne.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to fill out a learning agreement and send it to my coordinator. It took a few tries to get it signed but after it was signed it was very easy. My coordinator just enrolled me in all of the courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I would say so yes. It was hard to actually figure out which courses I was allowed to take but after that I didn't have to do anything.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I wished for some master second year courses (M2) that I wasn't allowed to take. 
I ended up getting a full semester of classes that followed the first semester of the master "from fundamental molecular biosciences to biotherapies" which I can recommend.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are good at French then take the bachelor classes because they are easier to get. If you don't want classes in French the master I went to was very nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took master courses but I didn't find them harder than a bachelor course at University of Copenhagen. The level was fine. 
I also had a lab course where I would say it was a bit easy because a lot of the other students didn't have a lot of lab experience.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching didn't really suit me. There is a lot of courses that only consists of 2 hour lectures and that is it. 2 hours was a long time for me and I had a hard time concentrating. I also didn't feel like I got the information in because there wasn't any reinforcements.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Fundamental molecular sciences 15 ECTS
Ateliers de biologie moléculaire et cellulaire 12 ECTS (jeg havde kurset på engelsk)
French language course 3 ECTS

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend ateliers de biology moleculaire et cellulaire. It is a lab course where you spend a lot of hours in the lab. The hours are usually from 9-17/18 monday to friday for 3 weeks so it is a lot of school. You are however only 8-10 students to 2 teachers. It is the first time I feel like I have really understood what I was doing while doing it when I was in the lab.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Most people get their danish phone plan cancelled after 3 months abroad and had to get a French one but that didn't happen to me.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food was a bit more expensive than I thought but otherwise it was good.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of sports both at the university and where I lived and it was very cheap and easy to register.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Every first sunday of the month Kapela Marna teaches a house dance class, first beginner and then advanced, at club djoon. It is called soulful sunday and it is amazing. such great vibes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would definetely recommend going to Bretagne and Normandy

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: In general it is a little hard to get contact to French students but if you can find some to live with that is a good way.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The French people are a bit more reserved because there is more hierarchy.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The fashion. A lot of people were hats, the fashion it definitely more bold.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It is important to call your teachers with madam and monsieur and not by their first name. It is considered rude. 
There is a lot of late hours. 
There is a lot of sports opportunities.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No I think this is good.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of new friends from different cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That I didn't fully understand the language.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
